paper.title: Dynamic Balancing for Model Selection in Bandits and RL

settings.name_in_paper: Online model selection among M base learners with candidate regret bounds (stochastic contexts)
unmapped: Meta-learner selects among M black-box base learners, each with a putative regret bound R_i(n) that may or may not hold; at least one base learner is well-specified
The learner knows the candidate regret bounds R_i (shape C d_i n^beta), M and the confidence delta
Regret is measured against the optimal policy value mu*_t of a policy class
settings.definition_quote: At each round t, a context xt ∈ X is drawn i.i.d. from some distribution, the learner observes this context, picks a policy πt ∈ Π, thereby playing action at = πt (xt ) ∈ A, and receives an associated reward rt ∈ [0, 1] drawn from some fixed distribution that may depend on the current action and context.

bound.expression_latex: \tilde O(\sqrt{MT} + (B^{1-\beta} d_\star^{1/\beta} + d_\star + M^{1-\beta}) C T^\beta)

symbols.d_star: d_i of the smallest well-specified learner
symbols.beta_R: exponent of candidate regret bounds R_i(n) = C d_i n^beta

conditions: R_i(n) = C d_i n^beta with 1 = d_1 <= ... <= d_M, beta in (0,1)
at least one well-specified base learner
tuning: b_i(t) and v_i set as in Theorem 1 from the candidate bounds

source.quote: Let Ri (n) = Cdi nβ , where 1 = d1 ≤ . . . ≤ dM , β ∈ (0, 1) ... Then the regret Reg(T ) of Algorithm 1 is bounded with probability at least 1 − δ for all rounds T ∈ N as Õ(√(MT) + (B^{1−β} d?^{1/β} + d? + M^{1−β}) CT^β).

results.notes: Text is from lossy pdftotext; exponents reconstructed and consistent with Corollary 2 at beta=1/2. The gap-dependent part of Theorem 1 was not recorded because its expression is unrecoverable from the source.

conditions: R_i(n) = C d_i sqrt(n) with 1 = d_1 <= ... <= d_M
at least one well-specified base learner
tuning: b_i(t) = max(2 C d_i sqrt(i), c sqrt(M ln(M ln t/delta)))/sqrt(t)

source.quote: Suppose the candidate regret bounds are given by Ri (n) = Cdi √n ... Then with probability at least 1 − δ, the regret of Algorithm 1 is bounded as follows Reg(T ) = Õ(√(MT) + (√B d?^2 + d? + √M) C √T).
